title: c1 major SE+security convergent: write_state is check-then-act — the exists()/read window skips the forward-only published check
description: Evidence: write.rs:61-70 gates the prior read on path.exists(); a file created between exists()==false and the rename clobbers a written published block (the headline immutability invariant, enforced nowhere else); exists() also returns false on stat errors, taking the same skipped path; a file deleted after exists()==true leaks READ-vocabulary tokens (restore-state-file) out of the WRITE API; security's TOCTOU nit converges (two concurrent writers on fresh .vsdd both skip the guard). Disposition: drop exists() — one fs::read up front, NotFound = no-prior, other IO errors map to write-shaped refusals; document or lock the remaining read-to-rename lost-update window. Owner: software-engineer. Validator: security.

comments.author: xqjG
comments.content: FIX LANDED (commit daacdc84): the write path drops check-then-act — one fs::read decides prior-versus-absent, NotFound is the no-prior case, every other IO failure refuses write-shaped (the read-token leak closed); the residual read-to-rename lost-update window is documented in the module doc rather than claimed away.
